thread:
jessica: FYI CS just escalated a p95/p99 regression after the runtime rollout. Affected tenants on canary (10%). p95 ~+30ms, p99 +180-220ms for text-generation calls. https://grafana.redwood/prod/runtime/2850001234 :frowning:
nikhil: Is that canary only? Which variant/version rolled?
jessica: Canary v2.14.0 -> v2.15.1. We flipped the scheduler ordering + a small timing-wheel tweak (PR #4821). Only canary nodes are on v2.15.1.
maya: Scheduler tweak rings a bell. We changed host->guest kernel selection to prefer batching throughput in mid-latency cases. Could cause odd queueing for >1k context.
samir: Pasted a quick tail of runtime logs from a canary pod, looks like enqueue delays spike then KV cache churn around the same window:
```
2026-02-18T14:02:11Z runtime[pid=1102]: enqueue request id=abc123 delay=4ms
2026-02-18T14:02:11Z runtime[pid=1102]: kvcache miss key=model/xyz/seqgt1024
2026-02-18T14:02:11Z runtime[pid=1102]: scheduler assign delay=198ms shard=3
2026-02-18T14:02:11Z runtime[pid=1102]: kernel-select chosen=quant-opt-llama latency-est=3ms
2026-02-18T14:02:12Z runtime[pid=1102]: enqueue request id=def456 delay=6ms
2026-02-18T14:02:12Z runtime[pid=1102]: scheduler assign delay=230ms shard=3
```
alex: Can you reproduce locally with a quick curl that hits the same code-path? If so we can attach traces. Try adding the X-Redwood-Debug header.
jessica: repro command I used:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Debug: 1" -d '{"model":"llama-13b","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -o /tmp/out.json -w "\n%{time_starttransfer}\n"
```
With that I see a few 200 responses whose time_starttransfer jumps to ~0.35-0.55s vs baseline ~0.18-0.22s. Repro consistent when prompt+context >1024 tokens.
nikhil: Did batching config change in v2.15.1? Something that could increase queueing windows?
maya: No direct batching change in that PR. But the timing-wheel change altered the tick granularity from 1ms -> 4ms for certain queues to reduce wakeups. That can amplify small delays into p99 tails when combined with kernel-selection jitter.
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] rollout v2.15.1 -> canary (job id=deploy/2026-02-18-14:00, commit=6b9f2d). 10 nodes updated, 2 failing health checks (restart).
samir: Quick experiment: toggled prefer-low-latency=false on one canary host. Immediately saw p95 drop ~18ms and p99 back to ~baseline in the next 2 min window.
alex: Nice. How did you toggle? CLI snippet?
samir: 
```bash
redwoodctl runtime update-config --host canary-12 --set scheduler.prefer_low_latency=false
redwoodctl restart canary-12-runtime
```
jessica: Confirming: I toggled the flag across 3 canary nodes in the cohort and CS reported the customer’s tail latency went back to normal. Starting to suspect timing-wheel tick granularity + prefer-low-latency=true combo.
maya: Two mitigation options: 1) revert timing-wheel granularity change in the v2.15.1 candidate and re-run canary; 2) flip prefer-low-latency default back to false and ship a follow-up that reintroduces finer granularity behind a feature flag.
nikhil: Let's avoid full rollback if possible. Plan: (A) Roll the prefer-low-latency default back for canary (fast toggle). (B) Add extra telemetry for queue_wait_ms and kernel_select_reason to correlate. (C) Bisect PR 4821 subchanges (tick granularity vs other tweaks).
support-bot: CS ticket #C-11234 updated: told customer we have a mitigation and will follow up in 2 hours. Please add any customer notes.
alex: I'll add per-request tags so we can trace kernel selection path: request.metadata.kernel_hint and exporter for queue_wait_ms. Also add a histogram for scheduler.assign_delay.
jessica: Can someone own the short-term flip for canary and update CS? I'll coordinate with CS and post findings.
samir: I'll flip the default on remaining canary nodes now (runbook: flip flag -> drain -> restart). ETA 10m.
maya: After that we do a controlled bisect: split canary traffic 50/50, revert the timing-wheel change on half, run synthetic with long-context prompts (seq>1024) and compare p95/p99. If stable, we can push a narrower fix.
nikhil: Sounds good. Add an incident blameless note and link to this thread in the postmortem.
jessica: Updated CS: mitigation applied, monitoring in progress, postmortem promised. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
